p.i: Et princeps Tyrio vestem prætexuit ostro.
Hæc eadem pugnas accendere protulit ære.
Hos iuxta Nepesina cohors, æquique Falisci,
Quique tuos Flauina sicos, Sabatia quique
Stagna tenent, Ciminique lacum, qui Sutria tecta
Haud procul, & sacrum phæbo Soracte frequentant:
Spicula bina gerunt, caput his cudone ferito
Stat cautum, Lycios damnant hastilibus arcus,
Hæ bellare acies norant. At Marsica pubes
Et bellare manu, & chelydris cantare soporem,
Vipereúmque herbis hebetare, & carmine dentem.
Æeta prolem Anquitiam mala gramina primam
Monstrauisse ferunt, taciúque domare venena,
Et Lunam excussisse polo, stridoribus amnes
Franantem, acsyluis montem nudasse vocatis.
Sed populis nomen posuit metuentior hospes
Cum fugeret Phrygios trans æquora Martia Crenos,
Mygdoniam Phoebi superatus peditine loton.
Maruuium veteris celebratum nomine Marri
Vrbibus est illis caput, interiorque per vdos
Alba sedet campos, pomisque rependit aristas.
Catera in obscuro fama, & sine nomine vulgi,
Sed numero castella valent: coniungitur acer
Pelignus, gelidoque rapit Sulmone cohortes.
Nec cedit studio vicinus sanguine miles,
Quem genuere Cales, non parua conditor vrbis
(Vt fama est) Calais, Borea quem rapta per auras
Orithyia vago Geticis nutriuit in antris.
Haud illo leuior bellis Vestina iuuentus
Agmina densauit venatu dura ferarum.
p.note: Fiscellú opp. Pinna opp. Auellæ opp. Frétani pop.

p.i: Qua Fiscelle tuas arces, Pinnámque virentem,
Pascuáque haud tarde redeuntia tondet Auella,
Marrucina simul Frentanis æmula pubes

page.notes: The verse is Silius Italicus, Punica, book 8, transcribed line by line; the marginal notes are placed beside their lines. Some notes are short and approximate in wording where the scan is faint, notably the notes beside the Marsi and Pelignorum lines. The final line of the scan is a half-visible line, read with doubt.
